profile_text.body:
Symbotic describes itself as a provider of end-to-end warehouse automation for retailers and distributors, built around robotics and AI software. The company says its systems combine dense storage, streamlined operations, and AI-enhanced software, and that they can be adapted to palletized goods, small quantity fulfillment, and omnichannel operations. According to its site, goods ranging from 1 lb (0.5 kg) and 2 x 6.4 x 5 in (5.1 x 16.3 x 12.7 cm) up to 60 lb (27.2 kg) and 36 x 24 x 16.2 in (91.4 x 61 x 41.2 cm) can be managed and fulfilled in their native packaging, with options for loose items and cold chain requirements.

The company positions itself as the software and key robotic innovator behind each of its solutions, and says this lets it avoid the limits it attributes to typical integrators, which it describes as constrained by their portfolio of technology partnerships. Symbotic calls itself a leader in industrial automation and in technology at large, and states that its purpose is to get the right goods to people who need them, when they need them.

Symbotic Inc. is a public company headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts, traded under the ticker SYM, with SEC CIK 0001837240. Its recorded litigation exposure is in Massachusetts, where 187 cases are counted.
